title: Coca-Cola's India Bottler Files IPO in Pure Shareholder Sell-Down
excerpt: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings' draft prospectus offers up to 997.5 million existing shares; its majority owner cuts its stake to about 45% and the company gets no fresh funds.
body:
• Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings, parent of Coca-Cola's largest bottler in India, has filed draft IPO papers with SEBI, according to the draft prospectus reported by Reuters.
  • The offer is entirely a sale of existing shares: majority owner Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings will sell up to 997.5 million shares, cutting its stake from 60% to about 45%; the company receives no fresh money.
  • Jubilant Beverages, which holds the remaining 40%, is not selling. No price band has been disclosed.
  • Revenue fell 9.4% to Rs 115.49 billion ($1.23 billion) in the year to March 2026, a decline the company linked to handing territories to other bottlers under Coca-Cola's refranchising strategy.

Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings, the parent of India's largest Coca-Cola bottler, has filed for an initial public offering that is entirely a stake sale by its majority shareholder, with no fresh money going to the company, draft papers showed, Reuters reported on Saturday.

The structure of the offer

The proposed IPO will see Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings offer up to 997.5 million shares — 99.75 crore shares — for sale, reducing its holding to about 45% from 60%, according to the draft red herring prospectus dated November 6. Jubilant Beverages, which owns the remaining 40%, is not selling shares. No price band was disclosed in the draft papers.

An offer structured this way is a monetisation, not a fundraise: the bottler's balance sheet gains nothing from the listing, while its parent converts part of a long-held stake into public-market stock. The filing adds to a string of multinational companies turning to Indian equity markets to realise value from their Indian units rather than raise new capital.

The business behind the filing

The company bottles Coca-Cola brands including Thums Up, Sprite and Maaza across 10 Indian states and four federal territories, mainly in southern and western India, and is the largest Coca-Cola bottler in India by concentrate volumes sold, according to the draft prospectus. Its wider network, as detailed in the filing coverage, spans 14 bottling plants, about 1.7 million retail outlets and 2,273 distributors, with a portfolio of 41 products as of June 30, 2026.

Its headline numbers softened last year: revenue fell 9.4% to 115.49 billion rupees ($1.23 billion) in the year to March 2026, a decline linked to handing some territories to other bottlers as Coca-Cola continues its refranchising strategy. The retained business has since grown again — revenue from operations at the retained units rose 20.46% year on year to Rs 4,310.17 crore in the three months to June 30, 2026, according to the filing details.

What happens next

The draft prospectus names Kotak Mahindra Capital, Citigroup Global Markets India, JP Morgan India, Morgan Stanley India, Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs (India) Securities and IIFL Capital Services as book-running lead managers, with KFin Technologies as registrar. Coca-Cola said in June it was exploring a potential listing of the bottler's parent in 2027, and Reuters reported in July that the company had appointed JPMorgan and Citi for the planned listing. SEBI's review of the draft papers is the next step; the price band and offer dates come only after that process advances.

For investors, the question the filing poses is a valuation one: a pure sell-down by the parent, into a business whose reported revenue fell last year on territory transfers, will test how much the market pays for scale in India's beverages market without any new capital going into the company.
